openingMessage: The most important thing in the world is family and love. Never forget that.
openingWhy: Every rule we run — the attendant who stays put, the tested atmosphere, the staged rescue — traces back to some kitchen table that got a phone call instead of a truck in the driveway. The standard was never for the client. It's for whoever is waiting on you tonight.
leadershipThought: Act like a professional at all times. Respect the environment. Be aware. Don't create distractions. Act like the person the client would want back tomorrow.

fieldNews.headline: The whole crew — November is the best month of the fall
fieldNews.detail: Matt Croom's mid-month audit: 94.6% of forms complete in November, up from 82% in August. Trailer inspections at 98.8%. Seventeen techs at 100% for the week.

fieldNews.headline: Joseph Popillion — held the job and used stop work over a leaking casing
fieldNews.detail: Shull Crawford 15OO 115H, Monday: gas showed when the valves opened. Hold point, a plan, the right people notified, and the disconnect stopped until the crew was comfortable.

fieldNews.headline: Ralph Forbes — clean trailer inspection at 5:03 AM, before the drive
fieldNews.detail: Wednesday, trailer 139: complete and clean before the Highway 176 crash. Doing it right can't stop a reckless driver, but it's why we never stop doing it right.

fieldNews.headline: Justin Pack — six days running with nothing to fix
fieldNews.detail: Hughes #1, Friday through Wednesday: complete daily each day, both cascade fields, every photo from that morning.

fieldNews.headline: Andrew Bailey — trailer 602 covered three days running
fieldNews.detail: Wednesday: three trailer inspections and two air jobs, complete throughout.

fieldNews.headline: Marcos Morales — clean H2S daily at St Elmo, supervision job closed out
fieldNews.detail: Wednesday: nothing for the review to flag, and the multi-day supervision job closed properly.

fieldNews.headline: Highway 176 fog crash, Wednesday morning: five miles from the shop
fieldNews.detail: A driver weaving between semis tried to pass in fog and dark. Ralph and Jimmy are both okay and home with family. Slow down to what you can see, back off the semis, and let the weaver go.

todaysChallenge: Your standard today protects people you'll never meet — the night crew, the pumper tomorrow, somebody's dad next month. Leave the location better because you were on it.
todaysChallengeSubtext: “A life is not important except in the impact it has on other lives.” — Jackie Robinson

specialFocus.title: Finish Strong: Same Fight, All the Way to the Holiday
specialFocus.why:
Jacob, last day of the week. Finish it strong. Monday started with Mike's message. Tuesday was partners. Wednesday, good habits spreading. Thursday, Highway 176, and Ralph and Jimmy went home to their families. Today we close the week the way we opened it, and get ready for Thanksgiving week.

“We're in the same fight together. We all want the best for our families and ourselves. We sacrifice for them, and we need their support too. Stay diligent, keep your head on a swivel, and watch each other's backs.”
— Mike Lyons

And the numbers say it's working. Matt Croom's mid-month audit came in Thursday: November is the best month of the fall.

📈 THE FALL IN NUMBERS: Matt Croom's audit
  • Overall form completion: 82% in August, 83% in September, 91% in October, and 94.6% in November so far. The best month of the fall.
  • Trailer inspections: 98.8% in November, up from 82% in September.
  • Readiness forms: 89%, up from 69% in September.
  • Day forms: 96% complete in November.
✓ THE WEEK'S HONOR ROLL: say these names
  • 100% for the week (Nov 12–18): Joseph Popillion, Ralph Forbes, Marcos Morales, Stefanie Kirschke, Jimmy Cooper, Jordan Lemmons, Humberto Salazar, Justin Pack, Luis Zarate, Trevor McKenzie, Andrew Bailey, Pablo Soto, Justin Fontenot, Josh Blassingame, Dermont Morgan, Bobby Fleming and BJ Caesar. Popillion and Kirschke: second perfect week running.
  • Ralph Forbes and Jimmy Cooper: 100% for the week, and home with their families.
  • This fall's turnarounds: Popillion, perfect all November and the strongest turnaround in the company. Morales, the biggest climb in the file since September. Morgan, three months of steady climb. Bailey, a perfect November. Brey Rasco, the biggest one-month jump. Jobe, back to September-best form on one of the heaviest loads.
  • Steadiest since September: Cindy Smith, Humberto Salazar, Ralph Forbes, Justin Pack, Robbie Henigan, Rolando Flores, Jordan Lemmons and Luis Zarate.
▲ FINISH STRONG: three for today
  • Finish the week the way you started it. Every form, every photo, taken that day. The last job counts the same as the first.
  • Nights, match the days. Day forms are at 96% this month. Night crews, that's the bar. Let's bring it home.
  • Write it the way it is. Stopped the job? Tick “utilized.” Something not right? A true “No” and the fix beats a “Yes” that isn't so.
Ten minutes: the week and Mike's words (2) · the numbers (2) · names (3) · finish strong (1) · the last job (1) · send-off (1).
specialFocus.standardLabel: Week 23: Operational Discipline Through the Last Job
standard: The last job gets the first job's attention. Same JSA, same gas checks, same hold points.
Every form, every photo, taken that day, before you leave the location.
Watch your partner the whole shift, not just the first hour.
Stop it when it's wrong, and write it down: tick “utilized.”
Plan the drive home like part of the job. Lights on, phone down, nobody drives tired.

scenarios.title: The Last Job Before the Holiday Week
scenarios.body: It's Friday afternoon, the last location of the week. Everybody's thinking about the weekend and Thanksgiving. The job's nearly done, and somebody says, “We're almost out of here, let's just wrap it up.” What does finishing strong look like right now? Same gas check, same hold point, same partner check, and the forms and photos done before the truck rolls. Jacob, ask the circle: what's the last thing you check before you leave a location?

questions: What's one thing you did this week that you're proud of?
Who on your crew had your back this week? Did you tell them?
Thanksgiving is Thursday. What's your plan to get there safe, and who knows your route?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: Finish the way we started: every form, every photo, every partner. Ralph and Jimmy went home to their families this week. Same fight, same team. We all go home for the holidays.
